target_customer: Import traders, consumer goods distributors and resellers in Tanzania; brands that supply them
problem: Small distributors lack credit and visibility into inventory and sales, and consumer goods supply chains in Africa are poorly digitized.
business_model: SaaS for sales teams plus lending and trade finance (interest and fees)
product_category: Supply chain software and trade finance

founders.name: Iain Usiri
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no further background; company site lists him as CEO.

founders.name: Calvin Usiri
education: Trinity University, double major in Economics and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Education and employer from the YC page; company site titles him Chief Product and Technology Officer.

founders.name: Kibet Martin
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder with the Usiri brothers by AgFunder News and Tanzanian press; the YC page and company site do not list him.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile sales, inventory and point of sale tooling for low connectivity markets, later a lending stack needing a Bank of Tanzania license.

defensibility.rationale: Transaction data from distributors underwrites credit, and it obtained a lending license from the Central Bank of Tanzania (AgFunder 2022); early software alone was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found through 2025; Tanzania Commercial Bank joined as a capital partner in April 2025 alongside Stanbic.

market_need_then: Distributors in Tanzania ran on paper and cash, and CPG brands lacked visibility into the informal reseller chain; financing gaps were the stated problem (TechCrunch headline 2022-11).

branding.name_origin: Ramani is the Swahili word for map; press says it maps an economy that global brands never reached (profile, not a founder statement).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical: Stock up now. Pay as you sell.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional recognition in Tanzanian business press, but no mascot, community or brand press found.

pivots.from: Sales, inventory and point of sale app for distributor sales teams
pivots.to: Trade finance and clearing for import traders and distributors
pivots.why: Credit was the monetized layer on top of the data (AgFunder 2022; company site now); no dated pivot statement.

outcome_analysis: Ramani started as software for distributor sales teams in Dar es Salaam and used the transaction data to lend to resellers. It raised an undisclosed seed in 2021 and a 32 million dollar Series A in November 2022, mixing equity and debt, and later added Stanbic and Tanzania Commercial Bank as capital partners. It is still active with about 70 staff per the YC page, and the lending license gives it a regulatory position.
notes: Series A is described as combined equity and debt, with the debt from undisclosed investors; Schreiber is described as angel by TechCabal and as co-lead by others. Founding year 2019 (press) versus 2020 (YC). Competitor searches found only 2022 or later sources (Sokowatch/Wasoko, MarketForce, TradeDepot), so the founding-time list is left empty. Calvin Usiri's brother Joel Usiri is COO on the company site; not recorded as founder. Press claims about MarketForce shutdown and a Wasoko merger are unverified.
